name_reason: Conforms to data_fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> with battle core-table prefix data_fd2_battle_*; descriptor 'job_allowed_items_table' accurately reflects the per-job equippable item-type lookup table and the 'table' suffix reflects the data type. No Ghidra address residue in the name. The '_table' name reads cleanly with no trailing hex.
purpose: Per-job equippable item-type lookup table: for each job id, lists which item-category (type) IDs that job is allowed to equip.
logic_summary: 29 rows x 7 bytes (uint8), indexed by job_id via accessor fd2_get_job_allowed_items_table_entry @ 0x4E53E which returns &table[job_id*7]. Each row holds up to 6 allowed item-type IDs in bytes 0..5 (0xFF = unused slot) plus a constant 0x01 row marker at byte 6 (not consumed). Sole consumer fd2_check_job_can_equip_item @ 0x1C1C3 scans bytes 0..5 (loop bound '5 < type_iter') comparing each against the item's 'type' field (item_effect struct offset +1, the byte fd2_get_item_effect_entry points at); a match means the job can equip that item. job_id logical range 0..0x1A (27 jobs, rows 0..26); physical 29 rows (203 bytes) ending exactly at 0x61955 where the next table begins, so rows 27..28 are reserved/extra past the accessor range.
datatype: const uint8[29*7] (203 bytes, .object3); 29 rows x 7-byte stride
element_semantics: Per row of 7 bytes: bytes[0..5] = up to 6 allowed item-type/category IDs (matches item_effect.type at struct offset +1; 0xFF = empty slot; e.g. 01=sword,04=bow,06=staff,15=rod,16=book), byte[6] = constant 0x01 row marker (unused by accessor/consumer).
comment_original_issue: Minor imprecision: original src comment said allowed IDs match 'the item-category byte at offset 0 of each item_effect entry'. The consumer actually compares against item_effect struct offset +1 (the 'type' field, which is the byte fd2_get_item_effect_entry returns a pointer to); offset 0 is the unknown_00 field. Refined the phrase to reference the 'type' field at struct offset +1.
notes: 0x6188a has no Ghidra code unit of its own; it is a labeled sublabel (symbol data_fd2_battle_job_allowed_items_table) at offset +0x28D inside an 856-byte undefined byte[856] block starting at 0x615FD (data_orphan_615fd_...), which spans several adjacent battle tables. The containing block has no plate; a data PLATE_COMMENT cannot be attached at the sublabel address and the shared orphan block should not be repurposed for this one table, so ghidra_plate_action=none. The accessor fd2_get_job_allowed_items_table_entry @ 0x4E53E already carries a detailed function plate describing this table, consistent with the refined src comment. Evidence: accessor body returns base 0x615FD + job_id*7 + 0x28D = 0x6188A + job_id*7; next symbol data_fd2_battle_weapon_attack_anim_pattern_ptr_table_21 @ 0x61955 -> length 203 = 29*7; xrefs_to(0x6188a) = single DATA read from 0x4e54b inside the accessor; no writers (const). Name kept; only the one comment phrase refined.
